text:
maria: Quick heads up — we're scheduling a rolling maintenance window in eu-central1 next Tue 02:00-06:00 UTC to replace 2 rack-level cooling fans and apply a NIC microcode update on a subset of GPU nodes. Impact: short node reboots and one-minute kube drains per node.

sam: ETA for each node drain?

maria: ~6-8 mins total per node (cordon + drain + reboot + health checks). We'll stagger to keep at least 70% GPU capacity across pools.

raj: Which pools are affected? is this touching dedicated-gpu-pool-3 and ondemand-gpu-euc1?

maria: Yes — primary targets are dedicated-gpu-pool-3 and ondemand-gpu-euc1-rackB. We will avoid touching reserved-critical pools (dedicated-sla) unless we hit an unexpected failure.

katie: Do we have capacity buffer for canary inference jobs? customers running high-SLA routes?

maria: We plan to shift canaries to us-west2 for the 4-hour window and throttle batch sizes for best-effort routes. Critical routes (tagged sla:high) will remain on dedicated-sla.

leo: How will we perform drains? please share the exact command snippet so SREs are consistent.

maria: Use the drain command with evict-local-storage and grace period overrides, e.g.:

```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-123 && kubectl drain gpu-node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60 --force
```

raj: We should also patch kube-proxy if NIC microcode requires kernel reload. Any kernel restarts?

maria: NIC microcode shouldn't require kernel update, just firmware handoff and NIC re-init during reboot. ops-sre will validate.

ops-sre: I'll run a preflight: verify NICs show stable link after re-init and run a short iperf test to the egress GW. Plan attached to runbook.

ops-sre: Runbook checklist (short):
- mark nodes in rotation pool
- patch one node in rackB as canary
- smoke test inference path (latency + tokens/s)
- roll remaining nodes at 1 node every 8 minutes
- regenerate KV caches for long-LRU models if needed

sam: Any network maintenance windows overlapping? we have a partner switch firmware update in the same DC at 03:00 UTC.

maria: Good catch — partner switch window is 03:00-03:30. We'll avoid draining the same racks during that half hour. Sequence: canary at 02:10, ramp, then pause 03:00-03:30, resume after.

katie: I'll update the status page and send customer notice. Message draft: "Planned maintenance in eu-central1 may cause transient API latency increases and short reconnections for some workloads between 02:00-06:00 UTC" — ok?

maria: LGTM. Add note about fallback to us-west2 for critical workloads and that no data will be deleted.

leo: Autoscaling behavior? will HPA or cluster autoscaler kick things weirdly during drains?

ops-sre: We'll disable scale-up for the affected node pools during the window to prevent noisy autoscaling. We'll set cluster-autoscaler scaling policies: scaleDownDisabled=true and maxNodes+1 for headroom.

raj: Capacity numbers? need to advise product for temporary quota adjustments.
maria: Before window: eu-central1 GPU capacity 320 GPUs. Expected during maintenance floor ~224 GPUs (70%). We can route up to 40% of queued jobs to us-west2; estimated extra cost ~+$3.6k for the 4-hour window (on-demand egress + GPU run).

sam: Can we reduce cost by using smaller batch sizes instead of cross-region routing for best-effort workloads?
maria: We'll do both: throttle batch size for best-effort jobs and reroute long-running canaries to us-west2. That keeps SLA routes local.

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance job created for 1967890123 by maria. Reminder set 24h prior and 1h prior.

status-bot: Incident/maintenance banner created: eu-central1 — cooling fan replacement + NIC microcode. Visibility: public.

katie: I'll run the customer email at T-24 and post the status banner at T-2h.

ops-sre: On the execution day, call will be on #eng-oncall and we'll have live perf dashboards up (latency, tokens/s, error rate).

maria: Thanks team. Action items:
- ops-sre: finalize runbook and canary node list (today EOD)
- katie: status + customer comms (today EOD)
- raj/Product: confirm quotas to alert customers programmatically (EOD)
- leo: ensure autoscaler flags set (1h before)

sam: +1. If anything unexpected, abort and fallback to full us-west2 routing. :thumbsup:

maria: Will post a short postmortem if we see >1% error spike. Otherwise we'll close the maintenance thread with PASS.
